topic: Chrome warns before insecure HTTP sites

scenes.title: Chrome now stops people at your door

items.headline: Chrome Now Warns Before Insecure HTTP Connections
Google Chrome is done warning you about insecure websites after the fact

caption:
Google Chrome HTTP warning checklist: 4 things every small business website needs now that Chrome warns visitors before insecure sites load.

On October 21, 2026, Google said Chrome now asks people for permission before it opens a website that isn't secure (HTTP instead of HTTPS). The setting is called Always Use Secure Connections. It's on by default for all Chrome users, and Google says Chrome is the first browser to do this. Your visitor sees a warning and decides whether to go back or continue.

Google says nearly 95% of desktop users see no warning in a typical week, because most of the web is already secure. If your site is one of the few that isn't, your customers get stopped before they ever see your menu, prices or booking button.

Check these four things today:
1. Your web address starts with https and shows the lock in Chrome.
2. Every link you share (Instagram bio, Google Business Profile, flyers, email signature) uses the https version.
3. Your booking, contact and checkout pages open without a warning.
4. Your security certificate is set to renew, so the lock never quietly disappears.

caption_drafts.explainer:
Google Chrome now warns visitors before opening insecure websites, and it matters for every small business with an older site.

On October 21, 2026, Google turned on Always Use Secure Connections for all Chrome users. Before a page without HTTPS loads, Chrome asks the visitor for permission to continue. Google says Chrome is the first browser to do this.

Most sites already pass. Google says nearly 95% of desktop users see no warning in a typical week. The sites that do trigger it now meet customers with a warning screen instead of a homepage.
